preconditions.description: The number of packages, n, is between 1 and 1000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(package_name) <= 40 for package_name in package_names)
preconditions.description: Each package name has between 1 and 40 characters.
Each package has at most 20 dependencies.

preconditions.expression: all(dependency in package_names for dependency in dependencies)
preconditions.description: Each dependency is one of the other packages.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 'cannot be ordered' or all(package_names[i] in return_value for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The output is either 'cannot be ordered' or contains all package names.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 'cannot be ordered' or all(return_value.index(package_names[i]) < return_value.index(package_names[j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if package_names[j] in package_dependencies[i])
postconditions.description: If not 'cannot be ordered', each package is installed after all its dependencies.

postconditions.expression: return_value == 'cannot be ordered' or return_value == sorted(return_value, key=lambda x: (package_names.index(x), x))
postconditions.description: If not 'cannot be ordered', the output is lexicographically first among valid orders.
